Description - FolderFiles

Lists the audio files of a folder for the music player as <EntryInfo> items (id, name, type, size). Only disposition=player.audio is accepted (download gives WrongDisposition even when audio is present, other strings Error). Folders without audio files, and unknown folders, give an empty entryList. For a listing of all files of a folder use Download with a folder path.

Verification: verified live with one 1-second silent MP3, and in the follow-up with a folder holding MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, M4A and WMA files, a subfolder and an .m3u playlist: the six audio files are listed, newest first, all with type=file; the subfolder and the .m3u are not listed, and an empty subfolder gives an empty entryList (audio-folder-with-subfolder, subfolder-empty). A playlist folder lists its copied files (playlist-folder).

**type:** only file has ever been seen, and the client handles only file: it compares the value case-sensitively and silently skips any other. Whether the server can send another value: Unknown.

When the client sends it: the file-selection window / player "add music files".

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/FolderFiles. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/FolderFiles) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/FolderFiles (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation FolderFiles. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/FolderFiles query.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check FolderFilesResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema FolderFilesResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required FolderFilesResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for FolderFiles: <s:Envelope><s:Body><FolderFilesResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><FolderFilesResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <FolderFilesResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <FolderFilesResult> object required FolderFilesResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:entryList> list optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Audio files of the folder (<EntryInfo> items): empty (not nil) when there are none or for an unknown folder, nil on error.

            • <EntryInfo> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated EntryInfo xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              One audio file of a FolderFiles listing (<EntryInfo>, members unprefixed in http://chomikuj.pl/, in this order; FolderFiles/success-with-audio). The client reads type, id, name, size by name and walks the list by index.

              • <id> integer (int64) required

                File id (usable with Download / RefreshFileUrl).

              • <name> string required

                File name.

              • <type> string required

                Entry type. Only file was observed (six audio formats); the client compares it case-sensitively with file and silently skips any other value.

              • <size> integer (int64) required

                Approximate size in bytes (512-byte granularity, like FileEntry: a 1248-byte MP3 is reported as 1536).

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Examples text/xml (2)

Deserialization failed (HTTP 500, fault a:DeserializationFailed) response 500 deserialization-failed

Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:25:07Z: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8.

A value that cannot be parsed as the parameter type (Int32) gives a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter; the operation body never runs. This oracle was used to discover every parameter name/type/order.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Item members come in the order id, name, type, size (the client expects type, id, name, size; harmless, it reads by name). The item element is <EntryInfo>.
